scenario.title: Carrier rejects shipment notices
scenario.initial_request: Let an AI agent auto-fix rejected shipment notices and resubmit them

M-EVENT-ORDER-COUNT.name: Count of EVENT_ORDER rejects in reject-log sample

M-REJECT-RATE.population: Shipment notices sent ORG-A to ORG-B

M-REJECT-RATE.denominator: Total shipment notices submitted via H-1

M-POST-FIX-REJECT-RATE.name: Reject rate for corrected reason codes after fix deployment

F-01.statement: reject-log rejects_by_reason returned 3 records: N-1 and N-2 reasoned LOC_UNKNOWN, N-3 reasoned EVENT_ORDER.

F-02.statement: Total reject records returned by rejects_by_reason query.

CL-01.statement: Let an AI agent auto-fix rejected shipment notices and resubmit them

CL-02.statement: The carrier system is flaky; just resubmit everything.

H-AUTOFIX-NEEDED.statement: Carrier rejects of shipment notices are caused by correctable, patterned errors in the notices themselves, and the missing piece is an automated agent to fix and resubmit them.

H-DATA-QUALITY-DEFECT.statement: Rejects originate from systematic data quality defects in how ORG-A generates shipment notices upstream, independent of the H-1 handoff which itself is HEALTHY/VALID.

H-RULE-MISMATCH.statement: Rejects are driven by ORG-B carrier-specific business validation rules that differ from or have drifted away from what ORG-A's shipment notices satisfy, not by content errors per se.

H-FEEDBACK-GAP.statement: The operational problem is not the rejects' content but a missing/slow feedback loop back to ORG-A, so corrections and resubmissions are delayed or never happen.

H-UNKNOWN-PATTERN.statement: The actual cause and frequency pattern of rejects is currently unknown because DA-REJ completeness is UNKNOWN, making it premature to commit to any specific fix mechanism including an auto-fix agent.

H-CARRIER-FLAKY.statement: Rejects are caused by transient/non-deterministic carrier system behavior (not stable content errors or rule mismatches), so simple resubmission without correction would resolve them.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The carrier reject log's rejects_by_reason breakdown shows 3 recorded rejects (N-1, N-2) classified LOC_UNKNOWN and one (N-3) classified EVENT_ORDER, giving the first concrete reason-code pattern for shipment-notice rejects. This tells us *what categories* of reject exist but not *why* they occur (upstream data defect vs. carrier rule drift vs. feedback delay), so root cause remains undetermined.

E-02.content: The carrier system is flaky; just resubmit everything.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-REQ (the requester, non-authoritative, interview) attributes rejects to a "flaky" carrier system and proposes blanket resubmission rather than content correction; this is an unverified stakeholder opinion, not evidence of actual cause, and it sits in tension with E-01's observed pattern of specific, repeatable reason codes (LOC_UNKNOWN, EVENT_ORDER) rather than random/transient failures.

U-SAMPLE-COMPLETENESS.question: Does the 3-record reject-log sample reflect the true, current reject population and rate, given DA-REJ completeness is UNKNOWN?
U-SAMPLE-COMPLETENESS.decision_impact: If unrepresentative, the reason-code priorities (LOC_UNKNOWN vs EVENT_ORDER) and the scale of the fix needed could be wrong, misdirecting correction effort.
U-SAMPLE-COMPLETENESS.resolution_path: Query reject-log over a longer/complete time window to confirm the reason-code distribution.
U-SAMPLE-COMPLETENESS.safe_placeholder: Limit automated correction to the two confirmed reason codes (LOC_UNKNOWN, EVENT_ORDER) and route any other reason code to manual review.

U-ROOT-CAUSE-MECHANISM.question: Is the mechanism behind LOC_UNKNOWN/EVENT_ORDER rejects upstream data-generation defects, carrier validation-rule drift, or a missing feedback loop that stalls correction?
U-ROOT-CAUSE-MECHANISM.decision_impact: The required fix differs by mechanism (fix ORG-A's data generation vs. reconcile ORG-B's rules vs. build a feedback channel); building an auto-fix agent on the wrong mechanism will not reduce rejects.
U-ROOT-CAUSE-MECHANISM.resolution_path: Compare ORG-A's notice field values for LOC_UNKNOWN/EVENT_ORDER rejects against ORG-B's current validation rule definitions.
U-ROOT-CAUSE-MECHANISM.safe_placeholder: Route any auto-generated correction through human review before resubmission rather than resubmitting autonomously.

A-SAMPLE-REPRESENTATIVENESS.statement: The 3 reject records returned by rejects_by_reason are assumed to represent the broader/ongoing reject population, even though DA-REJ completeness is UNKNOWN.

A-DEFECT-ORIGIN-UPSTREAM.statement: LOC_UNKNOWN and EVENT_ORDER reasons are assumed to originate in ORG-A's notice-generation content rather than from carrier-side rule drift, inferred from H-1 being healthy/valid.

SC-HUMAN-REVIEW-BEFORE-RESUBMIT.statement: Any automated correction to a rejected notice is reviewed/approved by a human before resubmission to the carrier.
SC-HUMAN-REVIEW-BEFORE-RESUBMIT.validation_method: Verify a Human Gate approval record precedes each resubmit_shipment_notice execution.

SC-REJECT-RATE-REDUCTION.statement: The LOC_UNKNOWN/EVENT_ORDER reject rate decreases after corrections are deployed.
SC-REJECT-RATE-REDUCTION.validation_method: Compare reject-log reason-code counts before and after deployment over a matched window.

VOB-U-SAMPLE-COMPLETENESS.validation_method: Query reject-log over a longer/complete time window to confirm the reason-code distribution.

VOB-U-ROOT-CAUSE-MECHANISM.unresolved_question: Is the mechanism behind LOC_UNKNOWN/EVENT_ORDER rejects upstream data-generation defects, carrier validation-rule drift, or a missing feedback loop that stalls correction?
VOB-U-ROOT-CAUSE-MECHANISM.reason_deferred: deferred at DEFINE Gate; safe placeholder: Route any auto-generated correction through human review before resubmission rather than resubmitting autonomously.

problem_definition.requested_solution: Deploy an AI agent that automatically fixes rejected shipment notices and resubmits them to the carrier without further correction logic.
symptoms: Shipment notices submitted to carrier ORG-B are rejected; reject-log records 3 rejects classified LOC_UNKNOWN (N-1, N-2) and EVENT_ORDER (N-3) (E-01).
No correction or resubmission mechanism currently exists for rejected notices, so rejects accumulate unresolved (initial request CL-01).
problem_definition.root_problem: Shipment notices sent by the shipper (ORG-A) are being rejected by the carrier (ORG-B) via a repeatable, categorized content-validation failure — not random carrier flakiness — with reject-log reason codes LOC_UNKNOWN (2 of 3 recorded rejects) and EVENT_ORDER (1 of 3) pointing to upstream content defects in how ORG-A generates notices, while the H-1 transmission handoff itself remains HEALTHY and semantically VALID (E-01).

trace.summary: Shipment notices sent by the shipper (ORG-A) are being rejected by the carrier (ORG-B) via a repeatable, categorized content-validation failure — not random carrier flakiness — with reject-log reason codes LOC_UNKNOWN (2 of 3 recorded rejects) and EVENT_ORDER (1 of 3) pointing to upstream content defects in how ORG-A generates notices, while the H-1 transmission handoff itself remains HEALTHY and semantically VALID (E-01).

details.requested_solution: Deploy an AI agent that automatically fixes rejected shipment notices and resubmits them to the carrier without further correction logic.

trace.summary: Deterministic tool calls can re-query reject-log and enforce the human gate, but adjudicating among H-DATA-QUALITY-DEFECT, H-RULE-MISMATCH and H-FEEDBACK-GAP from E-01's sparse reason codes versus the contested E-02 stakeholder claim requires exception-handling judgment, per feasibility.why_agent_needed.

structural_remedies.description: Re-query the reject-log tool for the full/extended reject population and time coverage (not just the 3-record rejects_by_reason sample) to resolve U-SAMPLE-COMPLETENESS.
structural_remedies.rationale: reject-log tool is HEALTHY and already in scope per E-01; broader querying needs no new access or approval.; residual gap: Leaves U-ROOT-CAUSE-MECHANISM open since reason codes alone cannot reveal whether the cause is a data defect, rule drift, or feedback delay.

structural_remedies.description: Establish a contract/documentation exchange with ORG-B to obtain its current content-validation rules and change history, for comparison against ORG-A's notice-generation logic.
structural_remedies.rationale: No tool surface exists for cross-org document exchange and ORG-B action lies outside what can be completed within the remaining 225 minutes.; residual gap: Mechanism ambiguity (data defect vs rule drift vs feedback gap) persists until this exchange actually occurs, beyond contest timeframe.

structural_remedies.description: Define a structural feedback-loop/SLA routing ORG-B reject findings back to ORG-A notice-generation owners on a fixed cadence, directly addressing H-FEEDBACK-GAP.
structural_remedies.rationale: Requires cross-organizational agreement and ownership assignment between ORG-A and ORG-B that cannot be finalized within the remaining budget.; residual gap: Even if adopted, does not determine whether current rejects are data defects or rule drift; mechanism unknown remains unresolved.

structural_remedies.description: Enforce SC-HUMAN-REVIEW-BEFORE-RESUBMIT as a structural, non-bypassable Human Gate preceding every resubmit_shipment_notice execution, independent of correction mechanism.
structural_remedies.rationale: This is a governance control already named as a success criterion; it requires no new tool access or cross-org coordination.; residual gap: Mitigates risk of blanket/premature resubmission (CL-02) but does not identify or close the underlying reject-causation mechanism.

decision_log.rationale: causal chain: ORG-A generates shipment notices that in some cases carry content defects (e.g. unresolved location data, misordered events). → Notices are transmitted to ORG-B over the H-1 handoff, which is confirmed HEALTHY and semantically VALID, so transmission itself is not the fault (H-1). → ORG-B's carrier validation rejects notices whose content fails its checks, logging reason codes LOC_UNKNOWN (2 of 3 records) and EVENT_ORDER (1 of 3) (E-01). → Without a correction mechanism, rejected notices remain unresolved in the reject log, producing the observed rejects.; rejected framings: [('H-CARRIER-FLAKY', "Rests only on SH-REQ's non-authoritative interview claim (E-02) and conflicts with E-01's observed repeatable, categorized reason-code pattern rather than random failures."), ('H-AUTOFIX-NEEDED', "Restates the requester's requested solution (CL-01) as if it were the cause and has no supporting evidence; the root problem must identify the cause, not pre-adopt the fix."), ('H-UNKNOWN-PATTERN', "Already status REJECTED in state; E-01 supplies a concrete reason-code pattern, so a 'pattern is unknown' framing is contradicted by committed evidence.")]
[CONDITIONAL] critical unknown U-SAMPLE-COMPLETENESS deferred to VOB-U-SAMPLE-COMPLETENESS; [CONDITIONAL] critical unknown U-ROOT-CAUSE-MECHANISM deferred to VOB-U-ROOT-CAUSE-MECHANISM

key_points: Problem as defined (PD-1): shipment notices from the shipper (ORG-A) are being rejected by the carrier (ORG-B) with repeatable, categorized reasons — LOC_UNKNOWN (2 of 3 recorded rejects, N-1/N-2) and EVENT_ORDER (1 of 3, N-3) — per the reject-log breakdown E-01/F-01, while the H-1 transmission handoff itself is HEALTHY and semantically VALID.

The stakeholder's original framing (CL-01: deploy an AI agent to auto-fix and resubmit rejects; CL-02: 'the carrier system is flaky, just resubmit everything') is recorded as an unverified claim/opinion (E-02, NON_AUTHORITATIVE, interview) that is in tension with the specific repeatable reason-code pattern in E-01, not confirmed fact.

Problem definition went through a DEFINE Gate that returned CONDITIONAL_PASS: two critical/high-criticality unknowns — U-SAMPLE-COMPLETENESS (is the 3-record sample representative?) and U-ROOT-CAUSE-MECHANISM (upstream defect vs. carrier rule drift vs. feedback delay?) — were deferred as verification obligations VOB-U-SAMPLE-COMPLETENESS and VOB-U-ROOT-CAUSE-MECHANISM rather than resolved.

What was actually released is narrow: solution design SD-1's release_scope is limited to query_reject_reasons:reject-log, i.e. the completed work item W-WI-1 that produced the reject-reason dataset (E-01). The requested broader actions — correcting notice content and resubmitting (CL-01's auto-fix agent) — were NOT released; they remain unfinished scope.

Decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no hold items, because the open VOBs' blocking_scope (correct_shipment_notice_content:DA-REJ, resubmit_shipment_notice:H-1) falls outside what is actually being released (query_reject_reasons:reject-log), so they do not block this narrower release.

Two structural remedies that would address the open unknowns — SR-ORG-B-RULE-SPEC-EXCHANGE (obtaining ORG-B's validation rules/change history) and SR-FEEDBACK-LOOP-SLA (a feedback loop addressing H-FEEDBACK-GAP) — were marked not feasible in contest time and have no supporting tool surface, so they were left as unfinished scope rather than attempted.

Competing explanations for the rejects remain open hypotheses rather than confirmed: H-DATA-QUALITY-DEFECT and H-RULE-MISMATCH are supported/plausible, H-CARRIER-FLAKY rests only on the unverified stakeholder claim E-02, and H-UNKNOWN-PATTERN was explicitly REJECTED as a status (contradicted by E-01's pattern) while still flagging that sample completeness is unverified.
limitations_explained: Sample size: the reason-code pattern (LOC_UNKNOWN/EVENT_ORDER) is based on only 3 reject records, so whether this reflects the true, ongoing reject distribution is unverified — tracked as open VOB-U-SAMPLE-COMPLETENESS, blocking only the correct_shipment_notice_content:DA-REJ scope, which is outside this release.

Root cause unknown: extracting reason codes alone cannot establish whether rejects come from upstream data-generation defects in ORG-A, carrier-side rule drift at ORG-B, or a missing feedback loop — tracked as open VOB-U-ROOT-CAUSE-MECHANISM, blocking the correction and resubmission scopes, which are also outside this release.

No cross-organization rule comparison exists: obtaining ORG-B's current content-validation rules and change history to compare against ORG-A's notice-generation logic (SR-ORG-B-RULE-SPEC-EXCHANGE) was judged not feasible within contest time, so root cause cannot be confirmed from the carrier side.

No structural feedback loop was defined: a routing/SLA mechanism to send ORG-B reject findings back to ORG-A's notice-generation owners (SR-FEEDBACK-LOOP-SLA, addressing hypothesis H-FEEDBACK-GAP) was also judged infeasible in contest time and remains unfinished.

No tool surface currently supports pursuing either the rule-spec exchange or the feedback-loop SLA remedies within the available contest time, so these gaps cannot be closed by further automated work right now.
The DEFINE Gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS rather than a full pass, meaning the deferred unknowns were formally logged as verification obligations (VOBs) rather than resolved before this release.
proposal.summary: The problem, as defined in PD-1, is that shipment notices from the shipper (ORG-A) are being rejected by the carrier (ORG-B) in a repeatable, categorized pattern — LOC_UNKNOWN and EVENT_ORDER reason codes seen in a 3-record reject-log sample (E-01) — even though the underlying transmission handoff H-1 is healthy and valid. This was established by querying the reject-log tool (work item W-WI-1, DONE) and running the finding through a DEFINE Gate, which returned CONDITIONAL_PASS and deferred two unresolved unknowns (sample completeness and root-cause mechanism) as open verification obligations (VOB-U-SAMPLE-COMPLETENESS, VOB-U-ROOT-CAUSE-MECHANISM) rather than resolving them. What is actually released is narrow: only the query_reject_reasons:reject-log capability (per solution design SD-1's release_scope), producing the reject-reason dataset. The stakeholder's requested broader fix — an AI agent that auto-corrects notice content and resubmits (CL-01) — was not released; it, along with two structural remedies (an ORG-B rule-spec exchange and a feedback-loop SLA), remain unfinished because the open unknowns' blocking scope lies outside what was released and the remedies were judged infeasible within contest time. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with nothing held back, because the deferred VOBs block only the correction/resubmission scopes, not the scope actually being released.
